meta.note: Each source was loaded and its words checked on the page or PDF on 17 October 2026. Quotes are excerpts; "…" marks left-out words. Notes say what each claim covers and whether it cites data. Naming is not measurement.

corridors.scope: Named in Kansas and Oklahoma. No official naming was found in Texas, Iowa or Minnesota.

sources.who: Jennifer Rapp, Deputy Director, Anti-Human Trafficking Unit, Office of Kansas Attorney General Derek Schmidt (written testimony to the Kansas House Committee on Federal and State Affairs)
sources.title: Testimony in Support of House Resolution 6038
sources.quote: …intersection of major federal interstates such as I-70 and I-35 make Kansas a prime spot for both sex trafficking and labor trafficking.
sources.note: Kansas only. 'Prime spot' cites no data. The same testimony says 'most trafficking in Kansas involves local children.' HR 6038 itself died on the calendar.

sources.who: Oklahoma State Senate press release (Sen. Frank Simpson, co-author of HB 2651)
sources.title: Truckers against Trafficking measure heads to governor
sources.quote: The I-40 and I-35 corridor makes Oklahoma a prime location for not only drug trafficking, but human trafficking.
sources.note: Oklahoma only; no data cited. An earlier Senate release (2012-04-25, quoting Rep. Sally Kern) made the same I-40/I-35 claim.

sources.who: Gov. Mary Fallin (Oklahoma), signing statement for HB 2651, as published by Sandite Pride News
sources.title: Governor Mary Fallin Signs Human Trafficking Bill
sources.quote: …major interstate highways like I-35, I-40 and I-44 mean human traffickers move sex slaves and others involved in forced labor through Oklahoma City.
sources.note: Oklahoma City. The statement also calls the metro 'a hotbed for human trafficking activity' with no data cited; the wording closely matches a 2015 KGOU article (2015-08-31) that leaned on a 2003 DOJ ranking of states.

corridors.scope: Named in Kansas and Missouri, and in general terms by a Nebraska trooper.

sources.who: Jennifer Rapp, Deputy Director, Anti-Human Trafficking Unit, Office of Kansas Attorney General Derek Schmidt (written testimony to the Kansas House Committee on Federal and State Affairs)
sources.title: Testimony in Support of House Resolution 6038
sources.quote: …intersection of major federal interstates such as I-70 and I-35 make Kansas a prime spot for both sex trafficking and labor trafficking.
sources.note: Kansas only. 'Prime spot' cites no data. The same testimony says 'most trafficking in Kansas involves local children.' HR 6038 itself died on the calendar.

sources.who: Rep. Elijah Haahr (Missouri), chair of the Missouri House human trafficking task force, quoted by The Missouri Times
sources.title: Haahr, Human Trafficking Task Force gear up to fight modern-day slavery in Missouri
sources.quote: What separates Missouri, we have an international airport, and two huge corridors on I-70 and I-44,
sources.note: Missouri. Says the corridors set Missouri apart; does not quantify trafficking on them.

sources.who: Lt. Monty Lovelace, Nebraska State Patrol, quoted by KLKN-TV
sources.title: At least 900 people are sold by human traffickers in Nebraska every single month
sources.quote: Traffickers will use major corridors such as I-80, I-70 … But that does not stop at all that it occurs in small towns
sources.note: General statement by a Nebraska trooper (I-70 does not cross Nebraska). He adds that trafficking also happens in small towns. The headline's '900 a month' figure comes from a nonprofit, not the patrol.

corridors.scope: Named in Utah (St. George to Salt Lake City) and from San Diego north to Las Vegas, in news reports quoting officials. No official Utah or Nevada document naming it was found.

sources.who: Nate Mudder, deputy chief of investigations, Utah Attorney General's Office, presenting to the Utah Legislature's Organized Crime Subcommittee; reported by Utah News Dispatch (Kyle Dunphey)
sources.title: Human trafficking in Utah happens daily and local police are under equipped, investigators say
sources.quote: …sometimes fueled by the state’s growth and the Interstate 15 corridor, a well-traveled route for both human and drug trafficking.
sources.note: Utah. Reporter's paraphrase, not a direct quote; the AG office's slides for that hearing (le.utah.gov/interim/2024/pdf/00002623.pdf) do not mention I-15. No data on I-15 cases given.

sources.who: Blair Barfuss, police chief, Dixie State University Department of Public Safety (former ICAC task force investigator), quoted by St. George News (Cody Blowers)
sources.title: Southern Utah ‘ideal’ for sex traffickers to find victims, AG’s office says
sources.quote: Interstate 15 is a major distribution corridor, and human trafficking follows the same routes
sources.note: Southern Utah. The same article cites a Utah AG's Office statement that victims are rotated, 'being trafficked from Las Vegas to St. George, Salt Lake City, Washington state, California and then back again' (that statement does not name I-15 but describes this stretch).

sources.who: Tim Coughlin, U.S. Attorney's Office in San Diego, quoted by CBS Los Angeles (KNX 1070)
sources.title: Feds: Border Patrol Checkpoints On SoCal Freeways To Curb Trafficking
sources.quote: Interstate 5 north, Interstate 8 east and Interstate 15 north to Las Vegas have been recognized as major transportation corridors for those involved in human trafficking,
sources.note: Southern California, out of San Diego. Does not say who 'recognized' the corridors or on what data; the story is framed around border checkpoints.

corridors.scope: Named in Texas (El Paso to Houston) and Louisiana. The often repeated claim that the Justice Department ranks it the No. 1 route has no traceable source.

sources.who: Charles A. McClelland Jr., Chief of Police, Houston Police Department (written testimony to the U.S. House Committee on Homeland Security field hearing 'Combating Human Trafficking in Our Major Cities')
sources.title: Written Testimony Before The House Committee on Homeland Security
sources.quote: …make this city a “perfect storm” for Human Trafficking, including but not limited to: … I-10 corridor which stretches from the east to the west coasts
sources.note: Houston. Lists I-10 among eight factors; no ranking. The widely repeated claim that the DOJ named I-10 the 'No. 1' trafficking route in the U.S. has no traceable DOJ source.

sources.who: Texas House of Representatives, H.R. No. 975 (82nd Legislature, by Rep. Parker), adopted 2011-05-30
sources.title: H.R. 975 – Recognizing the last week of January 2012 as Texas Human Trafficking Awareness Week (enrolled)
sources.quote: …the Department of Justice has identified Interstate 10 between El Paso and Houston as a major human trafficking corridor
sources.note: Texas, El Paso to Houston. Attributes the corridor label to DOJ without citing a document; none was found. PolitiFact rated a similar '25 percent of trafficking victims are in Texas' claim Pants on Fire (2014-01-29).

sources.who: Louisiana First Lady Donna Edwards, quoted in a Louisiana Department of Transportation and Development announcement
sources.title: LA DOTD participates in a national panel with state and federal executives on human trafficking
sources.quote: We know that Louisiana has two of the worst corridors for human trafficking, Interstates 10 and 20…
sources.note: Louisiana. SUPERLATIVE: 'two of the worst corridors' cites no data or ranking source. The speaker led the governor's office anti-trafficking push but did not hold office herself.

corridors.scope: Named in Maryland and New Jersey.

sources.who: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Maryland (press release)
sources.title: Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office Continues Fight Against Human Trafficking
sources.quote: The Interstate 95 corridor’s numerous hotels, rest stops, truck stops, and bus stations are prime locations for traffickers to exploit their victims.
sources.note: Maryland. No data cited.

sources.who: New Jersey State Police, Human Trafficking Resources page
sources.title: Human Trafficking Resources – New Jersey State Police
sources.quote: …New Jersey, with its dense population and strategic location along the Interstate 95 corridor, is particularly vulnerable to human trafficking’s growth.
sources.note: New Jersey. Undated page (WordPress record: created 2024-12-10, modified 2026-06-10). The same page says trafficking 'does not have to involve movement.'

sources.who: Lt. Gov. Aruna Miller (Maryland), quoted by MPower Maryland (University System of Maryland)
sources.title: State, Community Leaders Reaffirm Fight Against Human Trafficking
sources.quote: Maryland’s position along the I-95 corridor makes us especially vulnerable and places our communities directly in the path of trafficking networks
sources.note: Maryland. No data on I-95 itself; she cites 1,300+ child sex trafficking cases reported statewide 2013–2024.

corridors.scope: Named in Oregon and from San Diego north.

sources.who: Kieran L. Ramsey, Special Agent in Charge, FBI Portland Field Office, in a U.S. Attorney's Office (District of Oregon) press release
sources.title: Federal Law Enforcement Partners Commemorate National Human Trafficking Awareness Day
sources.quote: Due to the I-5 corridor, human trafficking remains a huge problem throughout the state of Oregon…
sources.note: Oregon. No case counts tied to I-5.

sources.who: Travis Ostrich, FBI Supervisory Special Agent, Portland field office, interviewed by Elkhorn Media Group
sources.title: In Plain Sight: FBI Agent reveals disturbing trends in human trafficking in Eastern Oregon
sources.quote: Human trafficking is a pervasive issue in Oregon, with the I-5 Corridor serving as a conduit for these crimes from Washington to California,
sources.note: Oregon (Washington to California). Same article says Oregon 'ranks among the top 20 states' for sex trafficking without naming the data source.

sources.who: Tim Coughlin, U.S. Attorney's Office in San Diego, quoted by CBS Los Angeles (KNX 1070)
sources.title: Feds: Border Patrol Checkpoints On SoCal Freeways To Curb Trafficking
sources.quote: Interstate 5 north, Interstate 8 east and Interstate 15 north to Las Vegas have been recognized as major transportation corridors for those involved in human trafficking,
sources.note: Southern California, out of San Diego. Does not say who 'recognized' the corridors or on what data; the story is framed around border checkpoints.

corridors.scope: Named in Ohio, Georgia and Florida.

sources.who: Ohio State Rep. Michelle Teska (Warren County), Ohio House of Representatives press release
sources.title: Teska Supports Increase to Penalties Against Human Trafficking
sources.quote: Warren County’s location along the major corridors of I-71 and I-75 puts us at a critical crossroads in the fight against human trafficking.
sources.note: Ohio (Warren County, between Cincinnati and Dayton). No data cited.

sources.who: Georgia Attorney General Chris Carr, quoted by WRDW-TV (Augusta)
sources.title: Taking action: Georgia targets Augusta’s human trafficking problem
sources.quote: human trafficking is so often a very transit-oriented type of horrific industry … This allows us to cover I-75, I-85, I-16 and I-20
sources.note: Georgia. Explains placing AG trafficking prosecutors in Atlanta, Macon and Augusta to cover these interstates; makes no claim about their relative volume.

sources.who: Florida Highway Patrol case list obtained and reported by News 6 / WKMG ClickOrlando (Erik Sandoval)
sources.title: Human traffickers, smugglers use this Florida highway the most, according to FHP
sources.quote: It showed they have intercepted 126 incidents around the state, half of them along I-75 – the longest stretch of interstate east of the Mississippi River.
sources.note: Florida. SUPERLATIVE headline ('use this Florida highway the most') rests on FHP data: 126 suspected trafficking AND smuggling incidents over five years, about half on I-75. Enforcement counts, not prevalence; the examples are smuggling, and an FHP trooper says 'we’re seeing it a lot more because we’re looking for it a lot more.'

corridors.scope: Named in Nebraska and at Reno, Nevada, where police also named the short I-580 spur to Carson City (not drawn separately).

sources.who: Lt. Monty Lovelace, Nebraska State Patrol, quoted by KLKN-TV
sources.title: At least 900 people are sold by human traffickers in Nebraska every single month
sources.quote: Traffickers will use major corridors such as I-80, I-70 … But that does not stop at all that it occurs in small towns
sources.note: General statement by a Nebraska trooper (I-70 does not cross Nebraska). He adds that trafficking also happens in small towns. The headline's '900 a month' figure comes from a nonprofit, not the patrol.

sources.who: Gov. Pete Ricketts (Nebraska), at a press conference, quoted by KMTV 3 News Now
sources.title: Nebraska acts as corridor for human trafficking
sources.quote: …that’s how a lot of human trafficking happens … Along Interstate 80, at hotels, gas stations and that sort of thing.
sources.note: Nebraska. In 2019 Ricketts and the Nebraska AG put trafficking-hotline posters in every I-80 rest area.

sources.who: Hunter Mercurio, public information officer, Reno Police Department, quoted by KOLO-TV
sources.title: RPD encouraging community education and awareness to help identify and report human trafficking
sources.quote: Being in that I-80 and that I-580 corridor, we are also a tourist town … traffickers will bring their victims across state lines for these big events
sources.note: Reno, Nevada. Ties trafficking to big events (Hot August Nights, Rib Cook-Off) reached via the corridor.

corridors.scope: Named in Oklahoma, Tennessee and New Mexico.

sources.who: Oklahoma State Senate press release (Sen. Frank Simpson, co-author of HB 2651)
sources.title: Truckers against Trafficking measure heads to governor
sources.quote: The I-40 and I-35 corridor makes Oklahoma a prime location for not only drug trafficking, but human trafficking.
sources.note: Oklahoma only; no data cited. An earlier Senate release (2012-04-25, quoting Rep. Sally Kern) made the same I-40/I-35 claim.

sources.who: Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (Director Mark Gwyn)
sources.title: The Geography of Trafficking in Tennessee 2013 (follow-up to the 2011 TBI/Vanderbilt sex-trafficking study)
sources.quote: I-40 encompasses 455 miles of roadway and provides access to 20 Tennessee counties … makes the delivery of a trafficker’s “product” to a john that much easier.
sources.note: Tennessee. Two consecutive sentences; the report argues highway access eases sex trafficking but offers no I-40 case counts. It also notes that many questioned whether the 2011 study overstated the problem. PDF dated January 2014.

sources.who: Lynn Sanchez, program director, The Life Link (Santa Fe nonprofit that co-leads the New Mexico Human Trafficking Task Force with the Attorney General's office), quoted by KRQE News 13
sources.title: Albuquerque City Hall now home to hotline for human trafficking victims
sources.quote: Truck stops, the fact that I-40 runs through here and I-25, New Mexico in general overall is considered a cooridor state,
sources.note: New Mexico (Albuquerque). Advocacy source; 'cooridor' is the outlet's spelling. Says New Mexico 'is considered' a corridor state without saying by whom.

corridors.scope: Named in Virginia’s Shenandoah Valley, West Virginia and Maryland, where an FBI task force is named after it.

sources.who: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Virginia (press release on a case brought by the FBI's I-81 Human Trafficking Task Force)
sources.title: Maryland Man Charged with Leading Multi-State Sex Trafficking Network
sources.quote: …identifying instances of human trafficking along the I-81 corridor in the northern Shenandoah Valley of Virginia, West Virginia, and Maryland
sources.note: Virginia/West Virginia/Maryland segment. A standing FBI task force named for the corridor; not a ranking.

sources.who: FBI Richmond Division (spokesperson Dee Rybiski), reported by The Northern Virginia Daily (Jake Zuckerman)
sources.title: FBI forms human trafficking task force along I-81
sources.quote: The Federal Bureau of Investigations announced Thursday it has formed a task force designed to stamp out human trafficking along Interstate 81.
sources.note: Northern Virginia segment; announces the I-81 Corridor Human Trafficking Working Group hosted by the FBI's Winchester office.

sources.who: Virginia Attorney General Mark Herring, quoted by WHSV-TV (Harrisonburg) on his billboard campaign
sources.title: Billboards Bring Awareness to Human Trafficking
sources.quote: Interstate 81 is a major thoroughfare … We know that human traffickers often use interstates to move around
sources.note: Virginia (Shenandoah Valley). Calls I-81 a thoroughfare and says traffickers use interstates generally; not an explicit I-81 corridor claim.

corridors.scope: Named in Alabama and Kentucky.

sources.who: Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall (news release)
sources.title: Attorney General Steve Marshall Promises “Relentless” Pursuit of Traffickers on Human Trafficking Awareness Day
sources.quote: Right here in Alabama, our interstates–I-20, I-85, I-10 and I-65 – are major routes for human trafficking.
sources.note: Alabama only. No data cited.

sources.who: Kentucky State Police Officer Jason Morris, quoted by WUKY (Karyn Czar)
sources.title: Truck Drivers Being Trained To Help End Human Trafficking
sources.quote: It’s going on every day down I-65 where I work. There’s no telling how many folks … are actually being victims of human trafficking
sources.note: Kentucky. A patrol officer's anecdotal observation; no data.

corridors.scope: Named between the Twin Cities and North Dakota, and in southwest Wisconsin.

sources.who: Moorhead (Minn.) Police Chief David Ebinger, reported by MPR News
sources.title: Moorhead officials ask for help to combat sex trafficking
sources.quote: …such cases are becoming more common in the Fargo-Moorhead area as traffickers travel Interstate 94 from the Twin Cities to North Dakota oil fields.
sources.note: Minnesota–North Dakota, during the Bakken oil boom. Reporter's paraphrase; anecdotal.

sources.who: Inspector Chris Sukis, Wisconsin State Patrol, quoted by WXOW-TV (La Crosse)
sources.title: Advocates urge awareness as human trafficking continues across Wisconsin
sources.quote: …we have Interstate 90 and I-94 … It’s a growing challenge because we have that interstate pipeline
sources.note: Wisconsin (Coulee Region). Speaks of exposure, not measured volume.

corridors.scope: Named in New Mexico and Denver. A Colorado anti-trafficking group calls the corridor idea a common misconception.

sources.who: Lynn Sanchez, program director, The Life Link (Santa Fe nonprofit that co-leads the New Mexico Human Trafficking Task Force with the Attorney General's office), quoted by KRQE News 13

sources.who: Mitch Morrissey, former Denver District Attorney, now criminal justice fellow at Common Sense Institute, quoted by The Center Square (Derek Draplin), republished by Kiowa County Press
sources.title: Human trafficking reaches high levels in Colorado
sources.quote: The Denver metro area has always been a hub … because of the intersection of I-25 and I-70 … The illegal products, including trafficked victims, come into Denver

PUSHBACK: Kara Napolitano of Combat Human Trafficking called the belief that much trafficking happens along the I-25 corridor 'a common misconception' ('Highways are not a root cause of trafficking'), KXRM via Yahoo News, 2024-02-28: https://www.yahoo.com/news/three-misconceptions-human-trafficking-colorado-015612351.html

corridors.scope: Named between Tampa and Orlando.

sources.who: Cpl. Alan Wilkett, Pasco County Sheriff's Office (leads its human trafficking task force), quoted by Fox News
sources.title: Inside law enforcement's efforts to end human trafficking
sources.quote: So he’s going to use the I-4 corridor. In fact, those corridors are so hot with human trafficking activity that, at times, we put together a task force
sources.note: Tampa area. 'So hot' is anecdotal; no data cited.

sources.who: Tomas Lares, described as a 'human trafficking expert', quoted by FOX 35 Orlando (Valerie Boey)
sources.title: Truckers accused of kidnapping women along I-95; FBI seeks possible victims in Central Florida
sources.quote: Central Florida, the I-4 corridor is targeted. And also our interstates, I-95, I-75. Folks are brought from New York, here to Florida, Miami, and from Atlanta...Tampa to Orlando,
sources.note: Advocacy voice, not an official. Also names I-95 and I-75 in Florida. Date is the article's last update.
